caption: The drawing depicts two fabric dolls positioned against a plain, light background with a faint shadow cast to the left side of the composition. The doll on the left is standing and has long brown hair, a face with minimal features, and wears a dark purple top with voluminous sleeves, a red skirt with a wavy black and white border, and beaded necklaces in various colors (including blue, red, and white). The doll on the right is sitting with brown hair that drapes over its shoulder and features a similarly minimal face. This doll is dressed in a grayish-blue top and a large, bright yellow skirt with black and tan outlines near the hem. It also has a beaded necklace of red, blue, and white tones, and both dolls have limbs made from a light beige or tan material. The surface on which the dolls rest appears slightly stained or watermarked in the lower left corner.
title: Dolls (Apache Women)
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
